about: One row per (system, run) in a verifiable-inference comparison, so every number sits next to the request shape, the hardware, the referee verifier, the negative controls and what the proof does and does not guarantee. check_row.py validates a row with the Python standard library.

system.name: <FlashProve | zkIE | DeepProve | ...>
system.commit: <40-hex commit the proof was produced at>
system.modified: <false, or a list of the files changed, e.g. a CPU port>

request_shape.request_length: <tokens in the request, e.g. the T= field>
request_shape.checked_positions: <range of output positions the proof covers, as the verifier prints it, e.g. 24..1023>
request_shape.proof_timing: <after generation over a given sequence | during generation>
request_shape.model: <model id or 'synthetic weights', and the commitment id>

referee.verifier: <the UNMODIFIED reference verifier of the system, binary + build command>
referee.verifier_source_digest: <the digest the verifier prints for its own sources, if any>

negative_controls.change: <e.g. flip byte N of the proof>

covers: <what a YES establishes for THIS run>
does_not_cover: <input provenance, decision authorisation, execution binding, served-model identity, ... as applicable>

checker.party: <who ran the referee verifier, and their relation to the system's authors>
checker.record_sha256: <sha256 of the full check record this row summarises>
